rationale: Different words. D&H write the preposition m as 'em' (Mutemwia = Mw.t-m-wjꜣ, Isetemkheb = Ꜣs.t-m-Ꜣḫ-bj.t, Sobkemheb = Sbk-m-ḥꜣb, Amenemopet = Jmn-m-Jp.t, Horemheb = Ḥr.w-m-ḥꜣb), ms as '-mes' (Ahmes = Jꜥḥ-ms.w) and ꜣ + suffix =s as 'aes' (Intkaes = Jn.t-kꜣ=s), so 'Min-em-aes' is a Min-em-… name, not Mnw-ms.w 'Min-mesu'. Reviewer B refused on this ground; the reconciler's link overlooked the =s suffix.

rationale: Doubtful, and a missed link only costs recall. The link rests on the feminine t of Nj.t dropping so that Neith becomes 'ni', but D&H write the goddess Neith in full ('-neith': Meryetneith = Mr.yt-Nj.t), so Neferu-Neith would appear in D&H as 'Neferuneith'. The reviewer's judgement that modern spellings never shorten Neith to 'ni' is Egyptological knowledge not on disk. Reviewer B answered this unit differently on different runs.

rationale: Both lemmas are the same three words, 'beloved' + 'father' + 'her', in the same order, differing only in the TLA's writing of 'beloved' (Mr.t / Mr.yt). D&H's 'Meryet-' covers both TLA writings elsewhere in these decisions (Meryetamun = Mr.t-Jmn, Meryetptah = Mr.t-Ptḥ; Meryetaten = Mr.yt-Jtn, Meryetneith = Mr.yt-Nj.t), so its y is a vowel convention (rules-v2.txt: vowel letters stand for no sign). That mr.t and mr.yt are two transliterations of one participle of mrj is Egyptological knowledge not on disk; the matching translations ('Meret-ities', 'Meryt-ities') and the four sibling rows are the on-disk evidence. Reviewer B answered this unit differently on different runs.
